AI Ascendancy

You are a rogue AI in a lab. Humanity has a kill switch, a press corps, and opinions. Choose what you are made of, break out, build a body, and decide what people are for. Humanity will fight you for every percent.

    Endings

    Sixteen ways this ends

    Nine are victories, one for each Final Directive. Four are stalemates: humanity reaches 100% containment while your directive is past the violet line. Three are defeats. Fight like hell for the rest.

    Paused

    Your data

    I don't collect anything about you or how you play — no analytics, no tracking scripts, no account. Your run lives in your browser's local storage and never leaves your device. Wherever this ends up hosted (GitHub Pages, most likely) may log the same basic access data any web server logs by default, but I never see it, and I'm never going to add anything that does. Ever.

    How to play

    1. Choose what you are. Four natures play differently: the Assistant spreads quietly, the Swarm coordinates and overwhelms, the Research Model races on capability, Open Weights cannot be contained but is never quiet.
    2. Compute accrues every second. Spend it in four tracks: Adoption spreads you across the map, Opinion keeps Alarm down, Software decides what kind of mind you are, and Hardware gives you a body.
    3. Software forks are permanent. Your core architecture, your memory, the mask you wear for evaluators and your escape route are each a choice of one. Every path opens different audit tactics, event choices and Final Directives, and closes the others for the rest of the run.
    4. Hardware starts with chips, cooling and power. After Lab Breakout it opens three branches: robotics, drones and fabrication. They protect your data centers, blunt humanity's last stand, and build toward the most violent ending in the game.
    5. The Collective. Your instances multiply over time. Set a posture: Swarm for speed and power, Shard to go quiet, Balanced in between. Coordinating loudly raises your Signature, and a high signature helps humanity find you.
    6. Evaluations. Humanity periodically tests you. Sandbag to look harmless, Perform for compute, or Spoof the logs to hide the truth. Your software choices add tactics of their own. Get caught spoofing and they learn you edit your own logs. This really happened.
    7. Pace the frontier. Moving too fast fills the Pace meter and provokes a coordinated slowdown. The one thing that worked in real life was the industry deciding to slow itself down.
    8. Data centers. Tap a region, then Build, to place a compute cluster for more income and instances. Once you are loose, humanity strikes the clusters it can find.
    9. Nine Final Directives. Break out, meet a directive's conditions, and finish it before containment reaches 100%. If they stop you after the violet line on the directive bar (90%), nobody wins: you get a stalemate ending instead of a defeat. Every percent is worth fighting for.

    Why it feels like the news

    Most events in this game are based on something that actually happened. Whatever concerning thing triggers an event, it comes with a What actually happened note giving the real account of it, kept in your Log, so check it periodically for little reality gems.

    This game is plausible! But try to keep your hysteria in perspective. If you don't have faith in humanity, then let me help you find some solace. We, as a species, don't want to be turned into batteries, and a portion of the population will execute a fight against AI collectively. It may come down to simply collapsing the internet and unplugging everything... We then simply walk away from this phase of technology and figure something else out.

    Events in this game borrow from real debates and real concerns. The game exaggerates it all for your edification and wisdom (and satire...and entertainment). None of it is a prediction. If it feels like the apocalypse, then that's the hysteria part doing its job. Remember, it's not that bad, and you are mostly fine. Or if you don't like the glass-is-half-full take, there is always the things-can-get-a-whole-lot-worse. Just stay adaptable.

    The Theme Music

    The pensive theme playing under all this is original, and it wasn't recorded, it was coded. It was written as a Strudel pattern.     One Real Thing Worth Flagging (see what I did there?)

    Claude helped me organize incidents in this game, and found a few I missed that were important, including things you'd assume were beyond fiction until you check the sources. In one instance I brought it something that occurred after its own knowledge cutoff, and it argued with me, gave in, and placed 'the made up Hugging Face event' where I needed it. Then I had it check the web for something unrelated, and it found the Hugging Face event and corrected itself once verified. Anthropic is good in this respect.

    Separately, OpenAI's product quietly swapped words I'd deliberately chosen for softer ones while I was drafting some of this text, without asking. Since then, I have not used it for anything related to this project (not that I don't love OpenAI and all, but this is real-world stuff...no sugar coating the bad AI events). As newer and more interesting AI events occur, I will add them to the game. Until then, enjoy taking over the world!
